heard: To survive the first spacewalk, Alexei Leonov had to bleed his oxygen. On March 18, 1965, the Soviet mission Voskhod II reached orbit with Leonov and Commander Pavel Belyaev. Roughly 90 minutes after launch, Leonov floated into the vacuum, tethered only by a slender line. But after 12 minutes outside, his suit ballooned and stiffened so much he could no longer bend his joints. His feet slipped out of his boots, leaving him unable to pull himself back through the airlock door. Without telling ground control, Leonov opened a valve to release his life-sustaining pressure just to squeeze inside. After a manual re-entry, the crew crash-landed deep in the Ural Mountains and spent two nights among wolves and bears. His suit had become a pressurized trap, showing why.
